_about.what: Knee — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.brief: What the coach SAYS out loud as the set begins: the position and the movement in one or two short sentences, no camera talk (the person has already placed the phone). Keep it under about 35 words — it is spoken while they get into position. Good: "Lie on your back, working leg straight. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out." Bad: "Stand 2.5 m from the camera at hip height" (set-up, not movement) or a paragraph. Leave it out and the coach says only the name and the target.
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling", "tolerance": 25 }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place, and how a crooked phone is levelled at calibration (a standing or sitting trunk is upright, a lying one is along the floor; kneeling makes no assumption). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; leave it out for the settings.json default. Good: 20–30. Bad: 5 (nobody stands that still) or 60 (the joint is hidden by then).
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken, "cooldown" ms before the same cue may repeat (rules included, so one that is true every rep is not said every rep); "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

sources.name: E3 Rehab — Exercises for knee pain
Elevate Rehabilitation — what a physiotherapist prescribes for the knee

moves.name: Wall sit
moves.summary: Quad endurance against a wall, at a depth your knees are happy with.
moves.setup: Camera side-on, 2–3 m away, roughly hip height. Back flat on the wall, feet a good step out from it, shoulder-width apart. Slide down to a comfortable depth — thighs level is the classic target, a shallower bend if the kneecap complains. Whole body in frame.
moves.brief: Back flat on the wall, feet a good step out from it, shoulder-width apart. Slide down to a comfortable depth and hold it there.
moves.why: From the side the camera reads knee angle and whether your shins are vertical (knees not past toes) — both invisible from the front.

guide.surface: A flat wall with nothing on it and a non-slip floor. Barefoot or grippy shoes.

points.t: Feet hip- to shoulder-width apart, toes pointing straight ahead, both feet flat with weight spread across the whole foot — heels stay down.
Feet far enough from the wall that when you slide down the shins are vertical and the knees sit directly above the ankles — usually about 50 cm.
Knees bent to 90°: thighs parallel to the floor, shins vertical.
Knees track in line with the second toe — not falling inward toward each other, not pushed out. (Facing the camera side-on, the coach cannot see this; check it yourself in a mirror once.)
Knees do not travel forward past the toes.
Hips at the same height as the knees, pressed back into the wall. Pelvis neutral — a small gap at the lower back is normal.
Whole back — sacrum, mid-back and shoulder blades — in contact with the wall. Do not let the upper body lean forward off it.
Shoulders relaxed and back against the wall. Arms hanging at your sides, crossed over the chest, or held straight out in front — never resting on the thighs, which unloads the quads.
Back of the head touching the wall, chin level, eyes forward.
Breathe steadily throughout; do not hold your breath as it burns. The hold ends when the knee angle or the back on the wall gives way, not when you decide to push through.

guide.stop: Pain builds behind or around the kneecap (a burn in the front of the thigh is expected; kneecap pain is not).

moves.enterCue: Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety
moves.tempo: Slide down over 2 s, hold, stand up over 2 s.
moves.progression: Longer holds; a weight on the thighs.
moves.regression: Shallower knee bend (much easier on the kneecap), shorter holds.
moves.contraindications: Kneecap pain. Around 90° is where the kneecap is loaded most, so start shallower — a quarter or half bend — and deepen only if it stays comfortable.

faults.label: Sitting too high
faults.tip: Thighs parallel is the classic target. Sitting higher than that is fine and easier on the kneecap — it is the hold time that builds the quad.

faults.label: Below 90°
faults.cue: Come up a touch — knees at ninety
faults.tip: Compression behind the kneecap is greatest around a right angle, and grows as you go deeper still. If the kneecap complains, sit higher rather than lower.

faults.label: Back off the wall
faults.cue: Press your back into the wall
faults.tip: Shoulder blades, mid-back and hips all stay on the wall; leaning forward shifts load to the knees.

faults.label: Knees past toes
faults.cue: Walk your feet out — shins vertical
faults.tip: Keep the shin vertical so the load stays in the quads, not the kneecap.

faults.label: Hands resting on thighs
faults.tip: Arms at your sides, crossed, or out in front — resting on the thighs takes load off the quads.

faults.label: Heel lifting
faults.tip: Feet flat, a good step from the wall; if the heels lift, walk the feet out a little.

moves.name: Heel slide
moves.summary: Knee flexion range after surgery or injury — measured in degrees, rep by rep.
moves.setup: Lie on your back on the floor, side-on to the camera at floor level, about 2 m away. The leg you are working should be the one nearest the camera. Start with that leg straight, other leg bent or straight, hips and shoulders flat.
moves.brief: Lie on your back, working leg straight, hips and shoulders flat. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out.
moves.why: From the side, hip–knee–ankle form a clean triangle in one plane, so knee angle is read directly, and the heel and hip staying on the floor are both visible as height changes.

guide.surface: Firm floor or exercise mat. Not a bed or sofa: a soft surface swallows the heel and the camera loses it.

points.t: Lie flat on your back, legs out straight, the working leg nearest the camera.
Hips square and level, both buttocks on the floor. The pelvis should not tip toward the working side.
Lower back relaxed against the floor with its natural small arch — do not force it flat, do not let it arch up.
Heel stays in contact with the floor the whole way; it slides, never lifts. A sock on a smooth floor or a plastic bag under the heel helps it glide.
Knee and toes point straight at the ceiling throughout. If the knee falls outward the movement rolls into the hip instead of bending the knee.
Ankle relaxed or gently pulled up toward the shin (dorsiflexed) — do not point the toes.
Slide until you feel a firm stretch at the front of the knee, hold, then push the heel away until the knee is fully straight and the back of the knee touches the floor.
Straight and relaxed, or bent with the foot flat if that is more comfortable for your back. Keep it still — it should not help.
Arms resting on the floor at your sides, palms down. A towel or strap looped around the foot is fine for an assisted slide: pull gently with both hands, elbows on the floor.
Do not push on the thigh with your hands.
Head resting on the floor or a thin pillow, looking at the ceiling. Do not lift the head to watch the knee — the camera does that for you.
Shoulders down and relaxed, not shrugged toward the ears.
Breathe out as the heel slides in, breathe normally during the hold, breathe in as the leg straightens.
2–3 s in, hold 2–5 s at end range, 2–3 s out. Slower is better after surgery.

guide.stop: Sharp pain, a sudden increase in swelling, or if the knee feels like it locks or gives way.

moves.tempo: 2–3 s in, hold 2–5 s, 2–3 s out.
moves.progression: Slide further as range returns; add a strap pull at the end.
moves.regression: Smaller slides; a plastic bag under the heel.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain, a sudden increase in swelling, or a knee that locks or gives way.

faults.label: Heel lifting off the floor
faults.cue: Keep your heel on the floor
faults.tip: The heel should slide, not lift. Lifting it turns the movement into a leg raise and loses the knee-bend.

faults.label: Knee falling out to the side
faults.tip: Keep the knee and toes pointing straight up as you slide, so the bend happens in the knee rather than the leg rolling outward at the hip.

faults.label: Hip lifting
faults.tip: Lifting the hip cheats the last few degrees. Keep the pelvis flat and accept the smaller bend for now.

faults.label: Short of the flexion target
faults.tip: Ease into the last few degrees on each rep — that is where range is gained. Pain up to mild is expected; sharp pain is not.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.cue: Slow — hold the bend for a moment
faults.tip: Take 2–3 seconds to slide in, hold the bend 2–5 seconds, then 2–3 seconds out.

faults.label: Lifting the head to watch
faults.tip: Craning to watch the knee strains the neck and tips the pelvis. The coach is watching the knee for you.

faults.label: Not straightening fully
faults.tip: Full extension at the end of each rep matters as much as flexion.

moves.name: Quad set
moves.summary: Tighten the thigh and press the back of the knee down. The first exercise after most knee surgery.
moves.setup: Sit or lie with the leg straight, side-on to the phone at floor level. A rolled towel under the knee is fine. Tighten the front of the thigh so the kneecap draws up, hold, relax.
moves.why: Almost nothing moves — the kneecap glides a centimetre. A camera cannot judge the squeeze, so this one is logged by hand.
moves.progression: Straight leg raise once the thigh can lock the knee.
moves.regression: Shorter squeezes, or with the knee slightly bent over a towel.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain in the joint, or a knee that will not straighten without swelling increasing.

faults.label: Knee bending instead of pressing down
faults.cue: Press the back of the knee down
faults.tip: The back of the knee should flatten toward the floor. If the heel lifts, the hip is doing the work.

faults.label: Letting go too soon
faults.tip: The squeeze has to last for the muscle to learn it. Count it out loud.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: Count out loud through the squeeze so the breath cannot stop.

faults.label: Pointing the toes
faults.tip: Pulling the toes up helps the thigh switch on; pointing them lets the calf take over.

guide.surface: Firm floor or mat, or a bed if getting down is hard.
guide.stop: Sharp pain inside the joint, or swelling that grows during the session.
guide.cannotSee: The squeeze itself — the phone sees a still leg. It confirms position only.

points.t: Leg straight, toes pointing up, heel resting on the floor.
Kneecap draws up toward the hip as the thigh tightens.
Sit tall or lie flat; no bracing with the arms.

moves.name: Straight leg raise
moves.summary: Lying on your back, lock the knee straight and lift the whole leg to the height of the other knee.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, about 2 m away, working leg nearest the phone. Other knee bent, foot flat. Lock the working knee, lift the leg until it is level with the bent knee, pause, lower slowly.
moves.brief: Lie on your back, working leg straight, the other knee bent with the foot flat. Lift the straight leg to about 45 degrees, then lower it slowly.
moves.why: From the side the leg is one line: its angle from the floor gives the lift, and the hip–knee–ankle angle shows whether the knee stays locked — the fault almost everyone makes.
moves.tempo: Lift 2 s, hold 2 s, lower 3 s.
moves.progression: Add a light ankle weight; pause longer at the top.
moves.regression: Lift lower, or start with quad sets.
moves.contraindications: Hip flexor pain or a lower back that arches and hurts on the lift.

faults.label: Knee bending on the way up
faults.tip: If the knee bends even a little, the hip flexors take over and the quad does nothing. Tighten the thigh before the leg leaves the floor.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Press the lower back gently toward the floor; keeping the other knee bent makes this easier.

faults.label: Dropping the leg
faults.tip: The lowering is half the exercise. Three seconds down, every rep.

faults.label: Lifting too high
faults.cue: Stop level with the other knee
faults.tip: Above the other knee the hip flexors take over and the pelvis tips. Height is not the point.

faults.label: Pushing off the other leg
faults.tip: Bracing through the other foot hides how much work the lifting leg is really doing.

guide.surface: Firm floor or mat, not a bed.
guide.stop: Pain in the front of the hip, or the back arching and hurting.
guide.cannotSee: The back arching, and whether the foot is turning out.

points.t: Knee locked straight before it lifts and all the way through.
Lift only to the height of the other knee — higher adds nothing.
Lower back stays close to the floor; other knee bent.

moves.name: Terminal knee extension (band)
moves.summary: A band behind the knee pulls it forward; you press the knee back to fully straight.
moves.setup: Loop a band around a solid anchor in front of you at knee height and around the back of the working knee. Step back until the band is taut with a soft knee, side-on to the phone. Straighten the knee fully against the band, hold a second, soften and repeat.
moves.brief: Loop a band around a solid anchor in front of you and around the back of the working knee. Step back until the band is taut with a soft knee.
moves.why: Side-on, the hip–knee–ankle angle reads the last few degrees of straightening directly, which is exactly the range this move is for.
moves.tempo: Straighten 1 s, hold 1 s, release 2 s.
moves.regression: Lighter band, or hands on a support.
moves.contraindications: A knee that locks or gives way, or pain at the back of the knee under the band.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Hips pushing back
faults.tip: The band should straighten the knee, not fold you at the hip. Keep the hips over the feet.

faults.label: Snapping the knee back
faults.tip: Push into straight under control. Snapping into hyperextension loads the back of the joint.

faults.label: Heel lifting
faults.tip: The heel stays down so the quad does the work rather than the calf.

guide.surface: Any firm floor; the anchor must not move.
guide.stop: Pain behind the knee, or the knee not straightening at all.
guide.cannotSee: Whether the kneecap is tracking straight.

points.t: Straightens fully against the band each rep.
Kneecap points straight ahead, not inward.
Upright — the knee moves, the body does not.

moves.name: Step-up
moves.summary: Step up onto a box with one leg and drive to standing tall on it, then lower with control.
moves.setup: A step or box 15–25 cm high, side-on to the phone with the working leg nearest. Whole foot on the step. Push through that foot to stand fully on the step, tap the other foot up, then lower slowly to the floor.
moves.brief: Stand in front of a step 15 to 25 cm high. Put the whole working foot on it, stand up through that leg, then step back down under control.
moves.why: The knee angle of the lead leg goes from bent to straight every rep, and a trunk that pitches forward to cheat shows up as the shoulder–hip line tilting.
moves.progression: Higher step; hold a weight; slow the lowering.
moves.regression: Lower step, hand on a rail.
moves.contraindications: Pain under the kneecap on the way down; poor balance without a rail.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Pushing off the back foot
faults.tip: The floor foot should be almost weightless. If you bounce off it, the lead leg is not lifting you.

faults.label: Dropping down the step
faults.tip: Coming down slowly is where the strength is built and the knee is protected.

faults.label: Step too high
faults.tip: If the knee passes much beyond the toes or the trunk folds, the step is too tall.

guide.surface: A stable step that cannot tip; a wall or rail within reach.
guide.stop: Sharp kneecap pain, or the knee collapsing inward.
guide.cannotSee: The knee drifting inward — that needs a front view.

points.t: Whole foot on the step; knee finishes straight at the top.
Knee tracks over the middle toes, not inward.
Tall through the lift; a little forward lean is fine, folding is not.

moves.name: Mini squat
moves.summary: A shallow squat to about a third of the way down, knees tracking over the toes.
moves.setup: Face the phone, feet hip-width, toes slightly out, hands on a chair back if needed. Bend the knees and sit the hips back a little, keeping the heels down, then stand tall.
moves.brief: Feet hip-width, toes slightly out, hands on a chair back if needed. Bend the knees and sit the hips back a little, keeping the heels down, then stand tall.
moves.why: Facing the phone shows both knees at once: the depth from each knee angle, and the classic fault — knees drifting toward each other — as the distance between them shrinking.
moves.progression: Deeper; hold a weight at the chest.
moves.regression: Shallower, or hands on the chair.
moves.contraindications: Pain under the kneecap at the bottom.

faults.label: Knees caving inward
faults.tip: Screw the feet into the floor so the knees track over the second toe. Caving loads the inside of the knee.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Heels lifting
faults.tip: Sit the hips back rather than driving the knees forward; the weight belongs in the whole foot.

faults.label: Weight on the toes
faults.tip: Rocking forward loads the kneecap. Feel the pressure across the whole foot.

faults.label: Going too deep
faults.cue: Small bend — a third of the way
faults.tip: A mini squat is a short range on purpose; depth is added later, once it is painless.

guide.surface: Firm floor, bare feet or flat shoes.
guide.stop: Kneecap pain, or the knee collapsing inward.
guide.cannotSee: How far the hips travel back — that is a side-view detail.

points.t: Track over the toes, staying apart at the bottom.
Only a third of the way down — this is a mini squat.
Heels stay down; weight through the whole foot.

moves.name: Sit to stand
moves.summary: Stand up from a chair and sit back down without using the hands.
moves.setup: A firm chair, side-on to the phone. Feet flat and slightly back, lean forward from the hips, stand fully tall, then lower slowly until you touch the seat.
moves.brief: A firm chair. Feet flat and slightly back, lean forward from the hips, stand fully tall, then lower slowly until you touch the seat.
moves.why: Side-on the knee angle runs from about 90° to straight every rep, so each stand is counted. Whether the hands helped is not reliably visible, so form is listed rather than judged.
moves.progression: Lower chair; arms crossed; hold a weight.
moves.regression: Higher seat, or a light push from the hands.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Pushing up with the hands
faults.tip: Cross the arms over the chest so the legs must do all the work.

faults.label: Dropping into the seat
faults.tip: The sit-down is half the exercise. Take three seconds and touch the seat lightly.

faults.label: Dropping into the chair
faults.tip: Falling into the seat skips the hardest and most useful part of the movement.

faults.label: Throwing the body forward
faults.tip: A controlled forward lean is right; a lunge of the head and shoulders is momentum.

guide.surface: A stable chair against a wall so it cannot slide.
guide.stop: Dizziness, or knee pain on the way down.
guide.cannotSee: The hands pushing on the thighs or the chair.

points.t: Flat, slightly behind the knees, hip-width apart.
Nose over toes to start the stand, then tall at the top.

moves.name: Standing hamstring curl
moves.summary: Standing tall, bend one knee to bring the heel toward the buttock, thigh staying still.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, hands on a wall or chair in front, working leg nearest the phone. Keeping the thigh pointing straight down, bend the knee to lift the heel behind you, then lower with control.
moves.brief: Hands on a wall or chair in front, working leg. Keeping the thigh pointing straight down, bend the knee to lift the heel behind you, then lower with control.
moves.why: From the side the knee angle gives the curl, and the thigh swinging forward — the way people cheat — shows as the hip–knee line leaving vertical.
moves.progression: Ankle weight or band around the ankles.
moves.regression: Smaller bend, or lying on your front.
moves.contraindications: Cramp or sharp pain at the back of the thigh.

faults.label: Thigh swinging forward
faults.tip: The hip should not move — only the knee bends. Squeeze the buttock to keep the thigh pointing down.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the lower back
faults.tip: Brace the stomach lightly so the back does not sway as the heel rises.

faults.label: Thigh drifting forward
faults.tip: If the thigh comes forward the hip is helping. Keep both knees level with each other.

faults.label: Short of a right angle
faults.tip: Bend until the knee is at least ninety; short curls miss the range that matters.

guide.surface: Firm floor; something solid to hold in front.
guide.stop: Hamstring cramp or a sharp pull.
guide.cannotSee: The back arching, and the foot turning in or out.

points.t: Thigh vertical and still; only the knee bends.
Heel travels toward the buttock, not out to the side.
Tall, light hands on the support.

moves.name: Seated knee extension
moves.summary: Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower.
moves.setup: Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest. Straighten the knee until the leg is horizontal, pause with the thigh tight, then lower slowly.
moves.brief: Sit tall on a chair. Straighten the working knee until the leg is horizontal, pause with the thigh tight, then lower slowly.
moves.why: Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight, and leaning back to help shows as the trunk line tilting away from upright.
moves.tempo: Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s.
moves.progression: Ankle weight; longer hold at the top.
moves.regression: Part range, or stop short of straight if it clicks.
moves.contraindications: Sharp pain under the kneecap near full straightening.

faults.label: Leaning back to help
faults.tip: Leaning back lets the hip flexors join in. Keep the trunk upright and the thigh on the seat.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Thigh lifting off the seat
faults.tip: A thigh that lifts turns this into a hip lift. Sit heavy and move only the shin.

faults.label: Letting the leg drop
faults.tip: The lowering builds the muscle. Three seconds down, every rep.

faults.label: No pause at the top
faults.cue: Hold two seconds at the top
faults.tip: The pause with the leg level is where the quad works hardest. Count it.

faults.label: Gripping the seat
faults.tip: Pulling on the chair braces the whole body and takes load off the thigh.

guide.surface: A chair high enough that the feet hang or just touch.
guide.stop: Kneecap pain, or the knee locking with a clunk.
guide.cannotSee: The thigh lifting off the seat.

points.t: Straightens fully with the thigh tight; toes pulled up.
Upright, hands resting on the seat edge, not gripping.

moves.name: Split squat
moves.summary: A stationary lunge: one foot forward, one back, lower the rear knee toward the floor and stand.
moves.setup: Take a long stride so the front foot is flat and the rear heel is up, front leg nearest the phone. Lower straight down until the rear knee is near the floor, then drive up through the front heel.
moves.brief: Take a long stride so the front foot is flat and the rear heel is up. Lower straight down until the rear knee is near the floor, then drive up through the front leg.
moves.why: The front knee angle counts the reps cleanly from the side. The knee drifting inward — the fault that matters — needs a front view, so form is listed here rather than judged.
moves.progression: Hold dumbbells; rear foot on a step.
moves.regression: Shorter stride, shallower, hand on a wall.
moves.contraindications: Kneecap pain in the front leg, or hip flexor pain in the rear leg.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Front knee caving inward
faults.tip: Point the knee where the toes point. If it falls inward, shorten the stride and go shallower.

faults.label: Knee shooting forward
faults.tip: Lower like an elevator, not a slide. The front shin stays near vertical.

faults.label: Stride too short
faults.tip: A short stride drives the front knee far over the toes and loads the kneecap.

faults.label: Wobbling side to side
faults.tip: Set the feet on two rails, not a tightrope, and the balance problem disappears.

points.t: Foot flat, shin close to vertical at the bottom.
Knee over the middle of the foot.
Heel up, knee lowers toward the floor without touching.

moves.name: Hamstring stretch (lying)
moves.summary: On your back, a strap around the foot, raise the straight leg until the back of the thigh pulls.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, working leg nearest. Loop a strap or towel around the foot, keep the knee straight and draw the leg up toward vertical until you feel the stretch. Hold.
moves.brief: Lie on your back. Loop a strap or towel around the foot, keep the knee straight, and draw the leg up toward vertical until the hamstring pulls.
moves.why: The leg angle from the floor shows how far up it is, so the timer only runs while the leg is actually held high.
moves.tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, ease out.
moves.progression: Take the leg higher; point the toes up.
moves.regression: Bend the other knee; stop lower.
moves.contraindications: Pins and needles down the leg, or back pain during the hold.

faults.label: Knee bending to cheat the stretch
faults.tip: A bent knee moves the stretch off the hamstring. Lower the leg until it can stay straight.

faults.label: Hip lifting off the floor
faults.tip: Keep the other leg and both hips on the floor; the stretch should be in the thigh, not the back.

faults.label: Other leg lifting off the floor
faults.tip: If the other leg rises the pelvis has tipped and the stretch is coming from the back.

faults.label: Bouncing into the stretch
faults.tip: A steady hold lengthens the muscle; bouncing makes it tighten to protect itself.

guide.stop: Nerve-like tingling, or pain in the lower back.
guide.cannotSee: The knee bending slightly, and the toes pointing.

points.t: Knee straight, leg held toward vertical.
Hips and shoulders flat on the floor.

moves.name: Quad stretch (standing)
moves.summary: Standing, hold one ankle behind you and draw the heel toward the buttock, knees together.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, one hand on a wall. Bend the working knee, hold the ankle behind you, and gently pull the heel toward the buttock with the knee pointing down. Hold.
moves.brief: One hand on a wall. Bend the working knee, hold the ankle behind you, and gently pull the heel toward the buttock with the knee pointing down.
moves.why: The knee angle from the side shows how far the heel has come up, so the timer runs only in the stretch position.
moves.tempo: Ease in over 5 s, hold, release slowly.
moves.progression: Tuck the pelvis under to deepen; no wall.
moves.regression: Hold the trouser leg or a strap; lie on your side.
moves.contraindications: Kneecap pain in the bent knee, or cramp in the hamstring.

faults.label: Knee drifting forward or out
faults.cue: Point the knee at the floor
faults.tip: Keep the two knees side by side. The stretch comes from the hip extending, not the knee flaring.

faults.label: Arching the back
faults.tip: Squeeze the buttock and tuck the tailbone under — that is where the stretch deepens.

faults.label: Holding the foot too hard
faults.tip: Pulling the heel hard into the backside compresses the kneecap. A firm stretch is enough.

faults.label: Leaning forward
faults.tip: Folding forward slackens the hip flexor and the stretch disappears.

guide.surface: Firm floor and something to hold.

points.t: Heel to buttock, knee pointing at the floor beside the other knee.
Tall, pelvis tucked, light hand on the wall.

moves.name: Step-down (eccentric)
moves.summary: Standing on a step on one leg, lower the other heel slowly toward the floor and rise again.
moves.setup: Stand on a step facing the phone, weight on the working leg, other foot hanging in front. Bend the standing knee to lower the free heel toward the floor, touch lightly, and press back up. Hips level throughout.
moves.brief: Stand on a step, weight on the working leg, other foot hanging in front. Bend the standing knee to lower the free heel toward the floor, touch lightly, and press back up.
moves.why: Facing the phone shows the standing knee angle for the count and, more usefully, the pelvis: the free-side hip dropping is the sign the outer hip muscles have let go.
moves.regression: Lower step, fingertips on a wall.
moves.contraindications: Kneecap pain on the way down.

faults.label: Hip dropping on the free side
faults.tip: Think of lifting the free hip as you lower. A dropping pelvis means the standing hip is not holding you.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Knee caving inward
faults.tip: Keep the standing knee over the middle of the foot as you lower.

faults.label: Dropping instead of lowering
faults.tip: The whole point is the slow lowering. If the heel lands with a thud, the step is too tall.

faults.label: Taking weight on the lower foot
faults.tip: The heel touches the floor and comes straight back. Weight stays on the top leg.

guide.surface: A stable step; a wall within fingertip reach.
guide.stop: Kneecap pain, or the knee collapsing inward.
guide.cannotSee: How far the knee travels forward over the toes.

points.t: Knee bends over the middle of the foot; heel stays down.
Both hip bones stay level as you lower.
